Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

dirty talk noun

also talk dirty, obscene language, obscenity, obscenities, filthy language, foul language, smut

modern

Traupman 304

sermō obscēnus

obscene talk

Both words are classical, and obscēnus has the sense “indecent, obscene” in Cicero (jocandī genus … obscēnum, Off. 1.104, Lewis & Short); we have found no classical instance of the phrase itself.

Other words

  • obscēna, obscēnōrum n. pl. — obscene things, said or done

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Quint. 8.3.38: sī obscēna nūdīs nōminibus ēnūntientur (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    To talk dirty is obscēna dīcere; Cicero: quodque facere turpe nōn est, modo occultē, id dīcere obscēnum est (Off. 1.127, Lewis & Short).

  • verba obscēna — obscene words, swear words

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. profanity

    Morgan–Owens’s phrase; Lucilius uses it of words of ill omen, the adjective’s first sense.

  • turpiloquium, turpiloquiī n. — obscene or immodest speech

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Tert. Pud. 17; Ambros. Fid. 5.10.110 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. profanity · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • quodque facere turpe nōn est, modo occultē, id dīcere obscēnum est

    and what is not shameful to do, provided it is done in private, is obscene to talk aboutCic. Off. 1.127 (Lewis & Short)

See also the finger, abuse, indecent.
